title: The Threshold Theorem
summary: Concatenated codes push the logical error rate down doubly exponentially when the physical rate is below a threshold.
objectives: Compute the logical error rate after k levels of concatenation of the three-qubit code.
Find the threshold as the fixed point of the error map, and say what happens above and below it.
Compute the number of levels and physical qubits needed to reach a target error rate.
Use the model p_L = (c p)^(2^k) / c and state the assumptions of the threshold theorem.
mission: One level of the three-qubit bit-flip code, with perfect correction, maps a physical error probability p to f(p) = 3p² − 2p³. Write f(p), and concatenated(p, k), the error rate after k levels (f applied k times). Write generic_rate(p, c, k) = (c·p)^(2^k) / c. Write levels_needed(p, target), the smallest k with concatenated(p, k) ≤ target, or None if the error rate never gets that low. Set p_th to the threshold of f. For p = 0.01 and target = 1e-15, store the number of levels in k_needed and the number of physical qubits per logical qubit (3 per level, so 3^k) in qubits.

prediction.question: The physical error probability is p = 0.6, above the threshold of the map f(p) = 3p² − 2p³. What happens to the error rate as levels of concatenation are added?
options: It decreases, more slowly than below the threshold
prediction.explanation: For p above 1/2 the encoded qubit is wrong more often than a bare qubit: f(0.6) = 0.648, then f(0.648) ≈ 0.69, and so on toward 1. The majority vote of three unreliable qubits is worse than a single qubit when each is wrong more than half the time. Only p = 1/2 stays fixed.

hints: concatenated(p, k) applies f to p, k times: loop k times with p = f(p), then return p. For generic_rate use (c * p) ** (2 ** k) / c.

levels_needed: if p is not below p_th the error rate never decreases, so return None. Otherwise start at k = 0 and apply f until the value is at most target, counting the steps. The threshold is the fixed point f(p) = p with 0 < p < 1: solve 3p² − 2p³ = p, which gives 2p² − 3p + 1 = 0.

k_needed = levels_needed(0.01, 1e-15). Each level replaces every qubit by three, so level k uses 3**k physical qubits per logical qubit. Check your values by printing concatenated(0.01, k) for k = 0, 1, 2, ...
